[RB-ALARM-REFERENCE#07] Alarm reference > Core and router alarms: - **`DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE`** (major, on the DNS node). Timeout rate above 5 percent. Means DNS degradation. It can lag the onset by minutes to an hour, or never appear, so check `core_kpis`. - **`CPU_HIGH`** (warning, on a router or core node). CPU load high. Brief spikes are normal. By itself it does not show an outage.
[RB-MICROWAVE-DEGRADATION#03] Microwave link degradation > Differential diagnosis: Versus the harmless background LINK_DEGRADED The network raises minor `LINK_DEGRADED` alarms on links all the time ("minor errored seconds, link still within SLA"). They last 5 to 30 minutes, flap, and the sites' KPIs do not move. ... Versus a fiber cut ... On a fiber link, a minor `LINK_DEGRADED` with falling optical power can precede a cut by up to an hour. ... Versus congestion ...
[RB-DNS-DEGRADATION#03] Core DNS degradation > Differential diagnosis: Versus a public holiday or other expected demand change A holiday also lowers traffic in every region, but latency does not rise, the dip lasts all day, it follows a business-versus-residential pattern, and an `external_events` row exists. In a DNS fault the dip lasts hours, latency rises, and the DNS KPIs are off. Versus congestion ... Versus a bad change ... Versus AMF or UPF trouble ...
[RB-DNS-DEGRADATION#02] Core DNS degradation > Signature in the data: Core KPIs on the DNS node. `query_success_pct` falls from about 99.9 to between 85 and 93. `resolution_ms` rises five to twenty times from its normal 8 to 15 ms. These two series are the direct evidence and sit in `core_kpis`, not in cell KPIs. Cell KPIs in every region, starting in the same step. ... What stays normal. ... A `DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE` alarm, severity `major`, on the DNS node. ...

result.markdown:
# Sluggish Data on S-SAH-009 Due to Core DNS and Microwave Link Degradation

- **Classification:** incident
- **Root cause:** core_degradation at `CORE-DNS-01`
- **Confidence:** medium (Core DNS degradation and link degradation are directly evidenced by alarms and alerts, but maintenance calendar and external events were not checked.)
- **Impact:** 2026-09-21 12:30 to 2026-09-21 21:04
- **Cause time:** 2026-09-21 12:35
- **Affected:** S-SAH-009, S-SAH-003, S-SAH-010

## Summary

Core DNS degradation caused nationwide DNS timeouts and traffic slowness, compounded by subsequent microwave link degradation on LNK-SAH-02-B.

Users experienced slow data on S-SAH-009 during two distinct windows yesterday afternoon due to DNS and microwave link degradation.

## Timeline

- 2026-09-21 11:12: Software patch CHG-2026-0056 applied on CORE-DNS-01. [CHG-2026-0056]
- 2026-09-21 12:30: DNS degradation alert ALR-0024 started across 48 sites. [ALR-0024]
- 2026-09-21 12:35: ALM-000365 raised major DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE on CORE-DNS-01. [ALM-000365]
- 2026-09-21 14:11: ALM-000365 cleared on CORE-DNS-01. [ALM-000365]
- 2026-09-21 16:37: ALM-000366 raised major LINK_DEGRADED on LNK-SAH-02-B. [ALM-000366]
- 2026-09-21 16:45: Microwave degradation alert ALR-0025 started for S-SAH-003, S-SAH-009, S-SAH-010. [ALR-0025]
- 2026-09-21 21:04: ALM-000366 cleared on LNK-SAH-02-B. [ALM-000366]

## Evidence

- S-SAH-009 dl_volume_mb dropped below baseline starting at 2026-09-21 12:30. [T3]
- ALM-000365 major DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE occurred on CORE-DNS-01 from 12:35 to 14:11. [ALM-000365]
- ALM-000366 major LINK_DEGRADED occurred on LNK-SAH-02-B from 16:37 to 21:04. [ALM-000366]
- Sites S-SAH-003 and S-SAH-010 share the microwave link LNK-SAH-02-B and experienced parallel latency spikes. [ALR-0025, T2]

## Hypotheses

1. **core_degradation** at CORE-DNS-01: confirmed. Major DNS timeout alarms and widespread DNS alerts confirm core DNS service degradation. [ALM-000365, ALR-0024]
2. **transport_degradation** at LNK-SAH-02-B: confirmed. ALM-000366 and ALR-0025 confirm microwave link degradation affected S-SAH-009 and siblings in the afternoon. [ALM-000366, ALR-0025]
3. **bad_change** at CORE-DNS-01: rejected. The 78-minute gap between change application and degradation onset rules out a direct bad change effect. [CHG-2026-0056, ALR-0024]

## Ruled out

- CHG-2026-0058: Software upgrade on CORE-UPF-01 did not correlate with any active alarms during its timeframe.
- CHG-2026-0056: Timing did not support bad change due to a 78-minute delay before the degradation began.

## Recommended actions

- Investigate CORE-DNS-01 stability and resolver performance during high load periods.
- Inspect microwave link LNK-SAH-02-B hardware and error logs to prevent recurrence of LINK_DEGRADED alarms.

## Sources

- `CHG-2026-0056`: software_upgrade on CORE-DNS-01 at 2026-09-21 11:12: Software patch 21.4.2 -> 21.4.3 on CORE-DNS-01 (resolver service restart)
- `ALR-0024`: ended alert from 2026-09-21 12:30: 48 site(s) (S-SAH-001, S-SAH-002, S-SAH-003, S-SAH-004 +44 more); core CORE-DNS-01; region-level SAH, SFX, SUD, TUN; metrics: latenc...
- `ALM-000365`: major DNS_TIMEOUT_RATE on CORE-DNS-01, raised 2026-09-21 12:35, cleared 2026-09-21 14:11
- `ALM-000366`: major LINK_DEGRADED on LNK-SAH-02-B, raised 2026-09-21 16:37, cleared 2026-09-21 21:04
- `ALR-0025`: ended alert from 2026-09-21 16:45: 3 site(s) (S-SAH-003, S-SAH-009, S-SAH-010); metrics: latency_ms
- `T3`: query_kpis(entity_type=site, entity_ids=['S-SAH-009', 'S-SAH-003', 'S-SAH-010'], metrics=['latency_ms', 'dl_volume_mb', 'prb_util_pct'], start=2026-09 -> Deviation in 6 of 9 series. Earliest onset 2026-09-21 12:30: S-SAH-009 dl_volume_mb below baseline.
- `T2`: get_topology(node_id=S-SAH-009, include=all) -> Depends on (child -> parent -> core): S-SAH-009 (site) -> LNK-SAH-02-B (microwave link) -> AGG-SAH-02 (agg router) -> CORE-UPF-01 (core upf)
- `CHG-2026-0058`: software_upgrade on CORE-UPF-01 at 2026-09-21 11:15: Software patch 21.4.2 -> 21.4.3 on CORE-UPF-01 (service restart)

## Verification notes

- [lookalike] CHG-2026-0056 was applied to CORE-DNS-01 at 11:12, but the degradation began at 12:30 (ALR-0024), 78 min later. A change takes effect when it lands, so this timing does not support bad_change. Consider a fault of the node itself.
